CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  June 2, 2025-5:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber
OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
  (Absent: Councilmembers Jones, Hampton, and Madison)
CLOSED SESSION  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting recessed at 5:03 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session items:

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Name of Case: Sustaita v. City of Pasadena
  Case No.: LASC Case No. 22STCV11885

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Name of Case: Youines v. City of Pasadena
  Case No.: LASC Case No. 22STCV11933

  CONSIDERATION OF INITIATION OF LITIGATION pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (one potential case)

  The above closed session items were discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:22
  p.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Cole.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  CouncilmemberJustin Jones (absent)
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison (absent)
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that the Item 14 (APPROVE THE
  ALLOWABLE USES AND CHARACTERISTICS OF ENTITIES
  ALLOWED TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS FOR THE BUILDINGS
  WITHIN HAHAMONGNA WATERSHED PARK ANNEX AREA) has
  been pulled from the agenda and will return at a future City Council

Council Minutes  1  06/02/2025
   meeting. He reported that Item 17 (AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF PASADENA ADOPTING THE TENANT PROTECTIONS OF
  THE ELLIS ACT, GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 7060 ET SEQ.)
  will also be deferred to a future meeting due to a lack of quorum of
  Councilmembers able to participate on the matter.
CEREMONIAL MATTERS Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation recognizing June 6, 2025,
  as Gun Violence Awareness Day, and spoke on the significance of
  working together to reduce gun-related crimes and supporting those
  who have been impacted by gun-violence. Lola Osborne, Deputy
  Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community Services, and Natalie
  Salazar, from Day One, thanked the City Council for the
  proclamation and emphasized the need to prevent gun-violence and
  support youth and community members.

  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident, expressed the need to provide
  financial assistance to those who lost their homes in the Eaton Fire.

  Rene Gonzalez, Pasadena resident, provided comments related to
  Measures I and J, and advocated for increased taxpayer
  accountability on funds spent by Pasadena Unified School District.

  Jeff Justice, Pasadena resident, provided comments regarding

  Heavenly hlughes, My Tribe Rise, advocated for the City to raise a

CONSENT CALENDAR  ADOPT A RESOLUTION APPROVING THE UPDATED SEWER
  SYSTEM MANAGEMENT PLAN AND AUTHORIZE THE
City Manager/ Executive LEGALLY RESPONSIBLE OFFICIAL TO CERTIFY AND SUBMIT
Director  TO THE CALIFORNIA STATE WATER RESOURCES CONTROL
  BOARD (Public Works Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the Sewer System Management Plan is exempt from
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
  California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Chapter 3, Article 5, Section
  15061(b)(3), and California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Chapter
  3, Article 19, Class 1, Section 15301, Existing Facilities;
  (2) Adopt a resolution approving the updated Sewer System
  Management Plan (SSMP) (Resolution No. 10131); and
  (3) Authorize the Legally Responsible Official (LRO) to certify and
  submit the updated SSMP to the California State Water Resources
  Control Board (SWRCB), and adopt any legally necessary interim
  updates as may be required by the SWRCB.

  Councilmember Cole expressed concerns regarding insufficient
  vetting of this proposed action, and advocated for it to be referred to
  the Municipal Services Committee for review and recommendation
  prior to City Council consideration. In response to questions, Greg
  de Vinck, Public Works Director, reported that the proposed item has
  a deadline for submission to the State Water Resources Control

  ROOSEVELT SCHOOL BUILDING AT 315 N. PASADENA
  AVENUE AS A LANDMARK (Planning Dept.)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that, pursuant to the guidelines of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), Article 18 (Statutory
  Exemptions), §15270, CEQA does not apply to projects which a
  public agency rejects or disapproves;
  (2) Find that the Roosevelt School at 315 North Pasadena Avenue
  does not meet any of the four Criteria for landmark designation
  pursuant to Pasadena Municipal Code (PMC) Section
  17.62.040.D.2; and
  (3) Disapprove the application for landmark designation.
  Recommendation of the Historic Preservation Commission: On
  April 15, 2025, at a Call for Review hearing, the Historic Preservation
  Commission (HPC) recommended by a vote of 5-4 that the City
  Council approve the designation of the Roosevelt School at 315 N.
  Pasadena Avenue as a Landmark under Criterion C of PMC Section
  17.62.040.D.2 as an example of a Mid-Century Modern style
  educational facility.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that the public hearing notice was posted
  and mailed on May 19, 2025. He also reported that 14 letters in
  support of the City Council approving the designation of Roosevelt
  School Building as a landmark and/or providing comments on the
  matter, 1 letter providing historical architecture evaluations, and 20
  letters in opposition to the City Council designating the Roosevelt

Council Minutes  9  06/02/2025
   building as a landmark and/or providing comments on the matter,
  and 1 letter from the applicant providing information on the Roosevelt
  story in the 1950s era of Pasadena, were received by the City Clerk's
  Office, distributed to the City Council, posted online, and made part
  of the public record.

  Jennifer Paige, Planning Director, provided introductory remarks on
  the item. Kevin Johnson, Principal Planner, presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the item, providing information on the criteria for
  landmark designation, the application background, the Historic
  Preservation Commission's decision, and an evaluation framework,
  and responded to questions.

  Rene Gonzalez, applicant, presented a Powerpoint presentation on
  how Roosevelt Elementary played a significant role in providing an
  accessible school and education environment, historical accessible
  features promoting inclusivity, and opportunities for alt students to
  learn at the location throughout the 1900s.

  Dr. Elizabeth Blanco, Pasadena Unified School District
  Superintendent and on behalf of the landowner, provided a brief
  background on the School District's housing project plan for the
  Roosevelt School building. Mark Hulbert, on behalf of the landowner,
  presented a Powerpoint presentation on standard school buildings
  throughout the 1900s, noting in his presentation that the design of
  Roosevelt was not distinctive. Stan Barankiewicz, legal counsel
  representing PUSD, advocated for the City Council to only consider
  the status of landmark designation based on Criterion C when
  deliberating on the information presented.

  Rene Gonzalez, applicant, stated that Roosevelt School has
  maintained architectural integrity throughout the history of the
  building, that it should continue to be preserved, and argued that
  other school sites can be utilized for School District's faculty housing
  project.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry regarding the
  historical relevance of the architecture of Roosevelt School, Planning
  Director Paige confirmed that staff analysis concluded that there is
  no relevance as neither of the two architects were significant in their
  works. In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry if PUSD
  had plans to reopen Roosevelt School, Superintendent Dr. Blanco
  reported that the school site would not reopen due to lack of
  adequate amenities (cafeteria, auditorium, proper classroom sizes,
  etc.). Councilmember Hampton expressed support for the staff
  recommendation, noting a lack of findings to support a landmark
  designation. He also acknowledged the historical value that
  Roosevelt School brings to the community, and advocated for the
  school district to install a meaningful display depicting the history of
  the school site as part of the new faculty housing development
  project.

  Councilmember Lyon expressed support for staff recommendation
  and stated that he also cannot make findings for landmark
  designation due to the many modifications made to the school
  building over the course of years. Vice Mayor Rivas and
  Councilmember Masuda both echoed similar sentiments and
  expressed support for the staff recommendation.

  Councilmember Cole stated that preserving the Roosevelt School
  building may not be the best way to honor the history of the school
  site and expressed his support for the staff recommendation.
